t:
No part of any appropriation contained in this or any other Act shall be available for the payment of the salary of any officer or employee of the Federal Government, who—
    (1) prohibits or prevents, or attempts or threatens to prohibit or prevent, any other officer or employee of the Federal Government from having any direct oral or written communication or contact with any Member, committee, or subcommittee of the Congress in connection with any matter pertaining to the employment of such other officer or employee or pertaining to the department or agency of such other officer or employee in any way, irrespective of whether such communication or contact is at the initiative of such other officer or employee or in response to the request or inquiry of such Member, committee, or subcommittee; or 
    (2) removes, suspends from duty without pay, demotes, reduces in rank, seniority, status, pay, or performance or efficiency rating, denies promotion to, relocates, reassigns, transfers, disciplines, or discriminates in regard to any employment right, entitlement, or benefit, or any term or condition of employment of, any other officer or employee of the Federal Government, or attempts or threatens to commit any of the foregoing actions with respect to such other officer or employee, by reason of any communication or contact of such other officer or employee with any Member, committee, or subcommittee of the Congress as described in paragraph (1).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that protecting "communication or contact" with Congress is a form of participation. But the communication is between federal officers or employees and Members or committees of Congress, all of whom are inside the federal government. The section is an appropriations restriction protecting federal employees who talk to Congress; it brings no outside party into any federal decision.
fable.s: any direct oral or written communication or contact with any Member, committee, or subcommittee of the Congress

opus.w: The provision only protects communication between federal employees and Members or committees of Congress, and both sides are inside the federal government. It looks like participation because it protects communication with lawmakers. But under the definition, contact between federal employees and Congress stays within the government, and no outside party is brought into a federal decision.
opus.s: prohibits or prevents, or attempts or threatens to prohibit or prevent, any other officer or employee of the Federal Government from having any direct oral or written communication or contact with any Member, committee, or subcommittee of the Congress
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that this is participation, because it protects "direct oral or written communication or contact" with Congress and punishes anyone who blocks that contact. That reading fails the gate test. Everyone involved is inside the federal government: the officers and employees doing the communicating, the officials who might retaliate, and the Members, committees and subcommittees of Congress receiving the communication. No state, tribe, company, expert or member of the public takes part in any federal decision.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section prohibits federal officials from retaliating against other federal employees for communicating with Congress. According to the definition, Congress is inside the federal government, so communication between federal employees and Congress is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outsiders. There is no requirement for consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this or any other Act shall be available for the payment of the salary of any officer or employee of the Federal Government, who— (1) prohibits or prevents, or attempts or threatens to prohibit or prevent, any other officer or employee of the Federal Government from having any direct oral or written communication or contact with any Member, committee, or subcommittee of the Congress
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text protects federal employees' right to communicate with Congress, it involves "participation" by outsiders (Congress). However, the definition explicitly states that Congress is INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, communication between federal employees and Congress is intra-governmental and does not constitute participation as defined. Furthermore, the text is a prohibition on retaliation, not a mandate for a participatory process like a hearing or advisory committee involving non-federal actors.
